abstract: We drive pretrained action-conditioned video world models through New York City starting from street-level imagery. For a query location we retrieve the nearest Google Street View panorama, reproject it along the capture heading, remove near-field vehicles, and insert a 3D vehicle rendered under a chase camera. A kinematic bicycle model converts throttle and steering into each model's action space. First-person models are conditioned on the vehicle-free frame, and the ego vehicle is composited from renders indexed by the controller's yaw relative to the camera. No model is fine-tuned, and each rollout runs on a single GPU.
models_lede: All models receive the same initial observation and the same controller trajectory; only the action adapter differs.

limitations: Only the first frame is observed. Content entering the view later is sampled from the model's prior and does not match the real street.

Quality is highest in roughly the first 15 s of generated time. Afterwards facades simplify into flat geometry, road texture streaks, and color shifts. Forward driving rarely revisits earlier viewpoints, so camera-aware memory does not counteract this.
The composited ego vehicle is a 2D layer. It is not occluded by, does not shadow, and does not interact with generated content.
Large heading changes away from intersections steer the camera into facades. Turn routes are only meaningful when the first frame is at an intersection.
